defects.title: REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES does not reach the nt_ twin, so the by-name channel clears only half of an ND kernel
defects.failure_scenario: build_registry() registers every mode=="nd" kernel twice -- once as `name` (ND face) and once as `nt_<name>` (NT face) -- and both _make_spec calls receive the SAME base meta dict. So the decorator route (@op(..., real_valued=True)) clears both twins, but the override route is `name in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES`, which only ever matches one of the two spellings. Measured on this tree (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP1/run2/attack2.py, sections C and D): with `catalog.REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES.add("ts_outlier_33")`, `build_registry().get("ts_outlier_33").non_root` is False (cleared) while `build_registry().get("nt_ts_outlier_33").non_root` is still True; same for a throwaway nd kernel (base False / nt_ True). A WP11 plugin that declares an ND kernel it does not own therefore re-admits it to searchable(include_boolean=False) on the ND face only, and silently not on the NT face -- the opposite of the design's "one declaration fixes both levers". It does not bite the declaration the design actually plans (in_sustain_mean/_stddev/_product are dt-face and have no nt_ twin, which is why nothing breaks today), so this is a trap for later packages, not a current wrong result.
defects.suggested_fix: In _make_spec, let an override on the base name cover the derived twin: `real = bool(meta.get("real_valued", False)) or name in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES or (face == "nt" and name.startswith("nt_") and name[3:] in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES)`. Add a test registering a throwaway `@op("nd", "cs", arity=1)` boolean kernel, putting only the base name in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES, and asserting both `get(n).non_root` and `get("nt_"+n).non_root` are False. If the current behaviour is deliberate instead, say so in the comment at catalog.py:395-400 so WP11 knows it must list both spellings.

defects.title: A name in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES that matches no registered operator is a silent no-op
defects.failure_scenario: REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES is only ever consulted as `name in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES` inside _make_spec; nothing checks afterwards that every name in the set was actually seen. Measured: `catalog.REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES.add("in_sustian_mean")` (one transposed letter) builds cleanly and leaves searchable(include_boolean=False) at 218 with no warning. The failure mode for WP11 is that the plugin believes it moved the GP vocabulary 214 -> 217 while it is still 214, and the only visible symptom is a search trajectory that differs from the intended one -- there is no error, no log line, and no test that would catch it on the plugin side either (the kernel simply stays non_root). The same silence hides a name that was legal but got excluded by EXCLUDED_KERNELS or skipped by _validate.
defects.suggested_fix: At the end of build_registry, before `return reg`, add `unknown = set(REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES) - set(reg._ops)` and either `warnings.warn(f"REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES names no operator: {sorted(unknown)}")` or raise ValueError (raising is safe today because the set is empty by default, so no existing run can hit it). Pin it with a test that adds a typo'd name and asserts the warning/raise.

defects.title: No test distinguishes "skips the probes" from "runs the probes and overwrites the result"
defects.failure_scenario: The design's §5 wording is explicit that _make_spec must SKIP the probes rather than override their result, and the implementation does (counted: a plain build calls _probe_distinct_values 244 times and _probe_constant_capable 29 times; with the three in_sustain stats declared it is 241 / 26). But nothing pins it. Mutation M7 -- rewrite _make_spec to run the try/except + trivial expression first and then do `if real: distinct, trivial = 10 ** 9, False` -- leaves tests/test_real_valued_flag.py and tests/test_catalog.py fully green (16 passed), i.e. the two synthetic-kernel tests pass identically whether the kernel was probed or not. That is the whole point of the declaration for a plugin whose kernel is slow, hangs, or crashes the probe, and it is exactly the regression a future refactor of _make_spec would introduce unnoticed. (13 of the 14 mutants I injected were caught; this is the only survivor. Harness: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP1/run2/mutate.py.)
defects.suggested_fix: Add a test whose fake kernel records that it was called -- e.g. `calls = []` and `def fn(x): calls.append(1); return (x > 0).float()` -- register it with real_valued=True, call build_registry(), and assert `calls == []` beyond the _validate smoke call (or, more simply, make the kernel raise on the (40, 9) float input the probes use and assert build_registry() still returns a spec with boolean_output False). A monkeypatched counter around catalog._probe_distinct_values / _probe_constant_capable works too and is what I used.

defects.title: catalog.DAILY_FIELDS and WP2's dailyfields.py field tuples will be two unsynchronised copies of the same 9 names
defects.failure_scenario: WP1 puts STORED_DAILY_FIELDS / DERIVED_DAILY_FIELDS / LOG_DAILY_FIELDS in catalog.py (correct per the design), while WP2 adds a separate STORED_FIELDS / DERIVED_FIELDS / LOG_OF in the new dailyfields.py, which the design forbids from importing catalog.py. The two are joined only by the literal spellings. If they drift -- say dailyfields.py spells it "ListAge" but catalog.py keeps "ListAge" and someone later renames one -- the name still PARSES (parser.name() consults reg.daily_fields, fed from catalog.DAILY_FIELDS) but dailyfields.resolve() has no entry for it, so the failure surfaces at engine time on a production run as a KeyError/ValueError inside a leaf reader, not at import or parse time. Nothing in WP1 or in the design's WP2 test list cross-checks the two sets. I verified the 9 spellings in catalog.py match the design's "The field set" section exactly, so there is no drift today.
defects.suggested_fix: In WP2's tests/test_daily_leaf_typing.py add a two-line guard: `from alphacube import catalog, dailyfields; assert catalog.STORED_DAILY_FIELDS == dailyfields.STORED_FIELDS and catalog.DERIVED_DAILY_FIELDS == dailyfields.DERIVED_FIELDS and catalog.LOG_DAILY_FIELDS == tuple(dailyfields.LOG_OF) and set(catalog.DAILY_FIELDS) == set(dailyfields.available(None)) | set(dailyfields.STORED_FIELDS)` (adjust the last clause to whatever available(None) returns). A test file may import both modules even though the modules themselves may not import each other.

result.notes:
VERDICT: approved. No high or medium defect. The commit implements all 8 design steps and all 6 listed tests faithfully, touches exactly the 4 files WP1 owns, and I could not make the default path diverge from the baseline in any way I tested.

SCOPE / HYGIENE
- `git diff --name-only 517fd09 1167f00` = src/alphacube/catalog.py, src/alphacube/operators/common.py, tests/test_catalog.py, tests/test_real_valued_flag.py. Nothing outside the owned list. Working tree of /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube-steering is clean; /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube stays at 517fd09 with an empty `git status --porcelain`; my scratch work is confined to /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP1/run2/ (gitignored, nothing committed).
- `real_valued=True` appears nowhere in src/ -- design step 8 ("apply the flag to nothing") is honoured.

(b) DEFAULT-PATH / RANDOM-STREAM IDENTITY -- the strongest evidence, and it is clean
I dumped a canonical snapshot from BOTH trees in separate processes (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP1/run2/dump.py, baseline via PYTHONPATH=/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src) and diffed every key:
- 244 specs x 17 attributes each (name/face/family/category/arity/requires_window/kernel_id/compute_axis/reduces_m/restores_m/lookahead/boolean_output/coarse_output/trivial_boolean/resource_risk/windows/non_root) -- IDENTICAL. Also the 50-entry `skipped` list, `fields`, `constants`.
- searchable() 240 / searchable(include_boolean=False) 218 / (+include_resource_risk=False) 214 -- unchanged.
- TypedTreeGenerator(reg, seed=7): 400 generated trees byte-identical, and the five `_rng.random()` draws taken afterwards identical (so no extra RNG consumption). gen.fields and gen.specs (214 names) identical.
- A second generator (seed=11): 240 mutate_subtree / mutate_window / mutate_constant / crossover results identical, plus the trailing rng draws.
- Vocabulary(reg): fields, windows and the 214 operator names identical.
Mechanically this is expected: the only non-default branch is `if real:`, and `real` is False for every kernel (REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES is empty, no call site passes the keyword); the else branch is the old code verbatim with the same short-circuit (`distinct <= 2 and _probe_constant_capable(...)`) and the same relative ordering against _probe_per_element_python. All three probes use their own torch.Generator().manual_seed(7/11/5) -- no shared or global RNG -- so skipping one cannot perturb another.

(c) NEW CODE PATH, EXERCISED
- Probes are genuinely skipped, counted by monkeypatching: plain build = 244 distinct-probe calls / 29 constant-probe calls; with the three in_sustain stats declared = 241 / 26.
- The comment's measurement is exact: declaring in_sustain_mean+_stddev+_product gives 221/217, and the per-kernel decrements are 219/215 -> 220/216 -> 221/217. `in_sustain` itself stays boolean_output and trivial_boolean when not declared.
- `real=True` sets distinct=10**9, so boolean_output False, coarse_output False (10**9 is above both the <=2 and the 2<x<=3 bands), trivial_boolean False -> non_root False -> re-admitted to searchable(include_boolean=False). Verified directly.
- `meta.get`, not `meta[...]`: confirmed necessary -- mutant M14 (`meta["real_valued"]`) blows up build_registry on the three manual binaries (pow/greater/less) and takes 6 failures + 7 errors with it.
- Baked variants inherit the base kernel's real_valued through `{**base, ...}` (ts_outlier real_valued=True -> ts_outlier_33 and nt_ts_outlier_33 both cleared). Reasonable, and the design is silent on it.
- Registry.fields and Registry.daily_fields are disjoint and parallel; none of the 9 daily names is a registered operator; default_full_catalog() specs are untouched by real_valued (they carry all three flags False already, so no new asymmetry).
- No caller is broken: `Registry(` has exactly one production construction site (catalog.py:448); no `@op(...)` call site in src/ passes more than `pair` positionally, so the new trailing keyword cannot be swallowed; nothing else reads the meta dict by anything but named keys (operators/__init__.py, fullcatalog.py:116), and no test asserts the meta dict's key set.

(d) TEST QUALITY -- mutation-tested, 13/14 caught
I copied the tree to a throwaway dir and injected 14 mutants (run2/mutate.py), running only tests/test_real_valued_flag.py + tests/test_catalog.py each time. Caught: op() dropping the key from meta; _make_spec ignoring the decorator flag; ignoring REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES; forgetting to clear trivial; pinning distinct into the coarse band (3) or the boolean band (2); Registry dropping the argument; build_registry not forwarding it; build_registry defaulting it to (); leaking daily names into `fields`; a one-letter typo in a daily field name; a daily name colliding with "Amt"; meta[...] instead of meta.get. Only survivor is defect 3 above. The pinned 29/22/0 sets and 218/214 counts in the new file are the first thing in the suite to pin them, which is the mis-flag tripwire the design asked for.
Test-pollution check: the fake-kernel fixture writes into the global OPERATOR_REGISTRY, so I forced the adversarial order (`pytest tests/test_real_valued_flag.py::test_real_valued_flag_skips_the_probes ::test_boolean_and_trivial_sets_pinned ::test_searchable_counts_pinned ...`) to make the fake kernel exist before the session-scoped `registry`/default_registry() singleton is first built -- still green, so the try/finally teardown closes that hole.

OBSERVATIONS THAT ARE NOT DEFECTS, FOR THE RECORD
1. The asymmetric default is deliberate and matches the design verbatim: `Registry(fields)` -> daily_fields == (), but `build_registry()`/`default_registry()` -> the 9 names. Both are now pinned by tests. WP2's parser branch reads reg.daily_fields off default_registry(), so it will see the 9 names.
2. `default_registry()` caches _DEFAULT, so a plugin that mutates REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES after the first default_registry() call has no effect (verified: late `add("eq")` leaves the cached spec non_root True while a fresh build_registry() gives False). The design puts the _DEFAULT reset in WP7's load_plugins, so this is WP7's responsibility, not a WP1 gap -- but WP7 must actually do it.
3. Cost: build_registry() is ~0.2-1.0 s depending on warm-up, and the new tests add ~12 build_registry() calls. Measured incremental cost of the two new test files together is ~3 s; the full suite ran 160 s here vs the design's documented 125.6 s baseline, which I attribute mostly to machine variance (I did not time the baseline tree, because running pytest there would write .pytest_cache/__pycache__ into the read-only baseline worktree).
4. Cosmetic: build_registry's continuation line at catalog.py:447 is indented one space past the open paren (E128); there is no flake8/ruff config or lint test in the repo, so nothing enforces it.
5. COMMIT ATTRIBUTION -- for the orchestrator, not a code issue. The task text required the final line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; commit 1167f00 ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. The implementer flagged this and explained the reasoning (its own harness reminder named Sonnet 5, and the computed task text was marked as carrying no user authority). I am only reporting the discrepancy: deciding which line this relay's record should carry, and whether to amend the commit message, is the coordinator's call -- please take it to the user rather than having an implementer resolve it, since the same conflict will recur in every WP of this relay.
